title: Grateful Dead Live at Ivar Theater on 1966-02-25

ai_review.summary: A raw‑early‑66 show with Pigpen blazing and a crystal‑clear soundboard capture, highlighted by King Bee > Caution, Good Morning Little Schoolgirl and the school‑girl jam.
ai_review.review: Fans rave about this mysterious 1966 recording for both its historic performance and surprisingly pristine audio.  The band is on fire – Pigpen’s harp and vocals dominate, Jerry delivers searing solos (especially on “I Know You Rider” and “Hey Little One”), and the school‑girl > You Don’t Love Me > school‑girl sequence is called a “petri‑dish” of early Dead experimentation.  The SBD source sounds almost CD‑quality for a mid‑’60s tape, making the whole set a must‑hear relic.

ai_rating.rationale: Over 30 reviews uniformly award 5 stars and praise both performance and sound quality; the few lower ratings are about dating controversy, not artistic merit.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Crisp, clear SBD tape with minimal hiss; reviewers note a tiny vocal‑mic distortion on Jerry but no drop‑outs.  Many call it “CD quality” for a 1966 recording.

standout_songs: Schoolgirl > You Don't Love Me > Schoolgirl jam
show_quality.setlist_flow: A hot, primal set that feels like a bridge between the early blues‑rock era and the later psychedelic explorations; transitions are tight and the energy never wanes.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Praised for razor‑sharp guitar tone, soaring solos on “I Know You Rider” and “Hey Little One”, and overall ‘wailing’ performance.
band_member_comments.Phil: Noted for strong bass work (some reviewers mention “great Phil”) that drives the bluesy feel.
band_member_comments.Keys: Early organ/keyboard adds a cheerful, blues‑filled texture; praised indirectly as part of the band’s raw sound.
band_member_comments.Drums: Bill Kreutzmann’s drumming described as masterful and driving the high energy of the show.
